explain.say: In 1820 Hans Christian Ørsted noticed a compass needle twitch whenever he switched on a current nearby. Electricity makes magnetism! On the board is how strong that magnetism is around a long straight wire carrying 10 amps, plotted against the distance from the wire.

explain.say: The field lines are circles wrapped round the wire. To find their direction, use the right-hand grip rule: point your right thumb along the current, and your curled fingers show the way the field circles. The strength, B, is measured in tesla. Do you expect the field to be stronger near the wire or far away?

explain.say: Near the wire. Ampère's law makes it exact: go round a closed loop, add up the field along it, and you get mu nought times the current passing through. For a circle of radius r, B times 2 pi r equals mu nought I, so B is mu nought I over 2 pi r. At 1 centimetre from 10 amps that's 200 microtesla. What happens at 2 centimetres?

explain.say: It halves, to 100 microtesla, because the field falls as one over r. At 4 centimetres it is 50 microtesla, about the same as Earth's own magnetic field, the flat line on the board. That's why a compass near household wiring can be fooled. Is this fall-off as steep as Coulomb's inverse-square law?

explain.say: No, gentler: one over r, not one over r squared. To make a strong field, wind the wire into a coil called a solenoid. Inside it, B equals mu nought n I, where n is turns per metre: 1000 turns per metre at 2 amps gives about 2.5 millitesla, and an iron core multiplies that hundreds of times. Superb! That's how scrapyard cranes lift cars, and MRI scanners reach 1.5 to 3 tesla.

faq.a: The line integral of the magnetic field round any closed loop equals mu nought times the current passing through the loop. It gives B wherever there is enough symmetry.

faq.q: What is the field around a long straight wire?
faq.a: B equals mu nought I over 2 pi r. It forms circles round the wire and falls off as one over the distance.

faq.q: What is the right-hand grip rule?
faq.a: Grip the wire with your right hand, thumb pointing along the conventional current. Your fingers curl in the direction of the magnetic field lines.
asks: How do I find the direction of the magnetic field?

faq.q: How strong is Earth's magnetic field?
faq.a: About 25 to 65 microtesla at the surface, depending on where you are. A 10 amp wire matches it at about 4 centimetres.
A long coil of wire. Inside it the field is nearly uniform, B equals mu nought n I, and an iron core can make it hundreds of times stronger.

facts: Hans Christian Ørsted discovered in 1820 that an electric current deflects a compass needle.
The permeability of free space, mu nought, is about 4 pi times 10 to the minus 7 henries per metre.

quiz.say: A long wire carries 5 amps. What is the magnetic field 2 centimetres from it?
quiz.show: A long wire carries 5 A. What is B at 2 cm from it?
quiz.why: B is mu nought I over 2 pi r: 2 times 10 to the minus 7, times 5, over 0.02, which is 50 microtesla.

wrong.1: That would be the field at 1 centimetre.
wrong.2: That would be the field at 4 centimetres.

quiz.say: If you move twice as far from a long straight wire, what does the field become?
quiz.show: If you move twice as far from a long straight wire, the field becomes...
quiz.why: B falls as one over r, so doubling r halves the field.

wrong.1: A quarter would be an inverse-square law, which applies to point charges, not long wires.
wrong.2: The field gets weaker with distance, not stronger.
